# Full mutation run: all 12,350 mutants of 7 files, 2026-11-22

**Scope:** every Mull-profile mutant (`cxx_default` + `cxx_remove_void_call`, generated by
`tools/mutation/mutants.py`) of `AudioLogic.cpp`, `CarCtrl.cpp`, `Cam.cpp`, `Frontend.cpp`,
`Ped.cpp`, `PedAI.cpp` and `Automobile.cpp`. These seven were chosen by size, change
frequency and spread across subsystems, not by Code Health (the CodeScene analysis of the
project is outdated); see the note at the end.

**Harness:** 19 scenarios (`tools/replay_harness/scenarios.txt`) x 3 seeds x 3000 frames;
trace hashes include game state, ped steering, traffic-AI plans, wheels and doors, camera
internals, audio requests and 2D draws. Each mutant ran the covering harness runs of its
line (up to 6), with `-harness-expect` stopping at the first differing frame.

**Execution:** `run.py --sample 0 --lanes 4`, 09:38-20:56 (about 11 h 20 min, about 1,090
mutants an hour), then a 267-mutant rerun (21:11-22:00, see "Baseline drift").

Raw data: `results.jsonl` (final, one line per mutant), `report.md` (every function and
operator, survivors), `coordinator-full.log`, `coordinator-rerun.log`, `bad_baselines.json`.

## Results

| File | Mutants | Killed | Survived | No coverage | Score | Covered score |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `src/audio/AudioLogic.cpp` | 1,862 | 710 | 257 | 895 | 38.1% | 73.4% |
| `src/control/CarCtrl.cpp` | 1,190 | 734 | 332 | 120 | 61.9% | 68.9% |
| `src/core/Cam.cpp` | 1,970 | 757 | 402 | 811 | 38.4% | 65.3% |
| `src/core/Frontend.cpp` | 1,511 | 158 | 172 | 1,181 | 10.5% | 47.9% |
| `src/peds/Ped.cpp` | 2,312 | 1,145 | 643 | 524 | 49.5% | 64.0% |
| `src/peds/PedAI.cpp` | 1,437 | 464 | 262 | 711 | 32.3% | 63.9% |
| `src/vehicles/Automobile.cpp` | 2,068 | 881 | 517 | 670 | 42.6% | 63.0% |
| **all** | **12,350** | **4,849** | **2,585** | **4,912** | **39.3%** | **65.2%** |

`score = killed / (killed + survived + no coverage)`, `covered = killed / (killed +
survived)`; 4 compile errors are left out (see below). Kills: 4,479 trace divergences, 199
crashes, 146 timeouts, 25 early exits.

| Operators | Score | Covered score |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| All | 39.3% | 65.2% |
| Without boundary (`<` to `<=` and so on) | 42.9% | 72.8% |
| Boundary only (1,676 mutants) | 16.4% | 23.8% |

Boundary mutants mostly compare floats, where hitting exactly the boundary value practically
never happens; many are equivalent in practice.

**Function verdicts** (ImageMagick gate on the covered score, at least 5 executed mutants):
259 functions qualify: **37 ready** (>= 90%), **67 careful** (75-90%), **155 not ready**.
309 functions have fewer than 5 executed mutants.

Ready, with the most evidence: `cAudioManager::ProcessPedOneShots` (95%, 63 mutants),
`CPed::Wait` (90%, 40), `CCarCtrl::ChooseModel` (100%, 33), `cAudioManager::ProcessCesna` (96%,
27), `CAutomobile::SetupSuspensionLines` (92%, 25), `CPed::SetEvasiveStep` (91%, 21),
`CCam::ProcessArrestCamTwo` (95%, 19), `CCam::FixCamIfObscured` (94%, 17).

Not ready, the biggest: `CAutomobile::ProcessControl` (64%, 342), `CAutomobile::PreRender`
(62%, 338), `CPed::ProcessControl` (58%, 325), `CCam::Process_FollowCar_SA` (69%, 251),
`CPed::ProcessObjective` (73%, 193), `CCarCtrl::GenerateOneRandomCar` (74%, 179),
`CPed::SetDirectionToWalkAroundObject` (62%, 125), `CCam::Process_FollowPed` (72%, 118),
`cAudioManager::ProcessPlayersVehicleEngine` (73%, 104), `CMenuManager::ProcessButtonPresses`
(60%, 100). These large functions are exactly the ones a Code Health campaign would split,
and the harness detects only about two thirds of the faults in them.

## Compared with the overnight sample

On the same 2,100 mutants as the overnight sample (`../2026-11-22/`): score 36.3% -> 39.5%,
covered 64.5% -> 65.3%, after the six new scenarios and the richer hashing. The sample
estimate of the covered score (64.5%) was close to the full figure (65.2%).

## Baseline drift

A first count gave 68.5% covered. A check then showed 267 kills from 29 unrelated functions
all diverging at the same frame (2809) of the two menu scenarios with seed 1. The
unmutated build diverged there too: the two baselines recorded at 10:42 no longer matched
the game's behaviour, while freshly recorded ones were repeatable. At that frame the menu
walk enters the Load Game page, which drew one 2D element fewer than in the morning; the
cause is not found (not the savegame folders, the skins folder, or the mouse cursor).
All other 55 baselines still matched. Those 267 mutants were rerun against fresh baselines:
243 survive, 24 are killed. The figures above include that correction; kills before frame
2809 of those runs, and survivors, were unaffected.

The overnight sample had the same artefact on a small scale: 7 of its 762 kills were at that
frame, from unrelated menu code; they survive in this run.

`run.py` now re-checks every baseline against the clean build at the end of a run and writes
`baseline_drift.json` (empty for the rerun).

## Other findings

- **Compile errors (4, all `CarCtrl.cpp`):** `-` to `+` between two pointers, which C++
  rejects. Mull works on IR and would not produce these; `mutants.py` should skip pointer
  differences.
- **Running instances side by side** needed two fixes, both documented in `../../README.md`:
  re3's system-settings broadcasts at start and exit deadlocked parallel instances, and
  opening the Windows default audio device stalled for over a minute (the tools now use
  OpenAL's no-output backend).

## Choice of files

The seven files were picked by size, git change frequency and spread across audio, peds,
AI, vehicles, traffic, camera and menu, without Code Health data. A campaign would pick by
CodeScene hotspots (low Code Health x high change frequency); once the project is
re-analysed, any hotspot not among these seven can be run with `run.py --lanes 4` in hours.
